expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: canceled variant contains only 'cancellation', no retry/grace fields; trialing has only 'trialEndsAt'; variants do not overlap

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: function assertNever(value: never): never { throw ... }; used in switch as default: return assertNever(sub);

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: Subscription type contains no id field; SubscriptionId type is never defined or branded

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: "The remaining concern is transitions... Put those behind a single transition function" but no implementation shown

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: "a trial cannot accidentally carry retry data, and a canceled subscription cannot omit its cancellation details"

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: "Use a discriminated union—not one object with optional fields"
